findings.what: The right answer is the first of the three choices on all seven puzzles, so by screen 4 Dan can answer by position alone; put it second or third on at least four of them, in STEPS and in the lesson's 'in this order' lists.

The picture under 'A board's drawing says TN-S' opens on TT, with the RCD and both electrodes drawn, which is the system of the third wrong choice; open it on TN with no fault (before: TN, after: TN with the fault) and drop `sets`.

Both TT electrodes land on the bar labelled 'Hull (earth)' and the text says the loop runs 'through the ground between them', but a steel hull is a conductor of a fraction of an ohm, so the picture tells a submariner his hull holds 110 Ω; say TT is a shore arrangement, a building with its own earth rod (in place of 'Both ends are earthed, so the fault has a way home.' to stay near 90 words), and label the bar 'Earth' on TT.

findings.where: Practice step 3 ('[^1]') and explain paragraph 3 ('This also counts as a form of IT.')
findings.what: Footnote [^1] (IET: 'I = Isolated') sits on 'I means isolated, or tied only through a high impedance', and no listed source says a high-impedance star point counts as I; add the EIG quote at research-notes.md line 738 ('...connected to earth through a high impedance (commonly 1500 Ω or more)') as a source and footnote that claim with it.

findings.where: Lead line above the stepper, and screen 1
findings.what: The lead 'An example 440 V three-phase supply, drawn as a star, feeds a motor whose frame is bonded to the hull.' stays above every screen and repeats screen 1's own sentences, adding 18 words to every SHOW screen (screen 1 reads 107 words with it, screen 5 reads 108); drop the lead or cut screen 1's repeat.

Nothing names the four buttons as 'the switch' or asks Dan to press them, and the screen has no read sentence for the read-through where the buttons are gone; add 'Tap TN, TT, IT and High impedance to move it.' (room made by the lead finding) with a read that leaves it out.

findings.where: Screen 1 and explain paragraph 1, the second letter
findings.what: 'The second is how the frames reach earth: N through a conductor back to the star point, or T through an electrode of their own.' is 25 words on a colon; split it, and say N stands for neutral, so the letter is as easy to keep as T for terre and I for isolated.

findings.where: Screens 3, 5, 7 and 9, 'tap Fault on L1' / 'tap the fault'
findings.what: Each demonstration strikes the fault by itself 0.4 s after the screen opens, so the instruction to tap asks for something already done; say 'The fault goes on by itself; Fault on L1 runs it again' in plain sentences, or let the tap start it.

Screen 2 draws TN with its protective conductor under 'A supply is marked IT', and screen 11 draws a floating IT star point under a supply whose RCD tripped, so each drawing reads as the supply in the question and contradicts it; add 'The drawing shows TN for now.' or open on a picture that is not one of the choices.
The third letter S is first met in the question and explained only behind Why?; give it one clause in a hint or on screen 1, or ask about TN without the S.

The read '... 508 A flows, and the breaker trips.' drops the 0.5 Ω loop it comes from, and the picture does not label 0.5 Ω, so the read-through gives the number without its working; add 'Say that metal loop is 0.5 Ω, so 254 ÷ 0.5 = 508 A.'

The screen carries two ideas, why a ship wants no trip and the high-impedance demonstration, and 'unearthed two-wire distribution' names two wires under a three-wire picture without a word on why; leave screen 9 to the high impedance and keep the why-ships point and its 'two-wire' source in the explanation and screen 10.
Six footnote markers, with [^5] twice and one on the bold summary, is more than a few for one lesson; drop [^3] (the frame bonded to the hull) and the [^5] on the bold summary.

'This is the first half of why the same fault on a ship's insulated 440 V supply disconnects nothing.' never says what the other half is; cut 'the first half of' or name the other half in one sentence.

findings.where: Motion when the switch leaves TT (by hand on screens 3 to 9, or a right Check on screen 12)
findings.what: The RCD, its electrodes and the old earthing vanish at once while the new earthing fades in over 0.6 s, so the outgoing parts blink out; fade them out over the same time.

The three dashed drops from L1, L2 and L3 sit 7 units apart and join in a short dashed bracket against the breaker or RCD box, which at 360 px reads as one dashed smudge rather than a path from each line; spread them further apart.
'L3' ends against L3's riser at x = 104 at 360 px; anchor it a few units further left.
